newsitem.title: USA: NASD warns muni dealers on PAC,party contributions.
newsitem.headline: NASD warns muni dealers on PAC,party contributions.

text.p: National Association of Securities Dealers warned muni bond dealers to use extreme care when making contributions to political action committees and political parties, according to an NASD mailing to firms.

Members should exercise extreme diligence to determine the ultimate beneficiaries of the political contributions," NASD said in its quarterly Regulatory & Compliance Alert, which will reach municipal bond dealers this week.
"Firms that aren't vigilant may find themselves" barred from doing negotiated municipal underwriting business with the particular municipality involved, NASD said.
NASD said before dealers give to a party or PAC, they should find out what the group is doing with the money it receives.

"If the party or PAC uses the money to support only one or two candidates who are issuer officials, firms may find themselves banned from doing business with those issuers for two years," the report says.
NASD enforces the rules enacted by the 15-member Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, a quasi-regulatory group that reports to the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Enacted in April 1994, the MSRB's controversial "pay-to-play" rule G-37 bars municipal bond dealers that contribute to issuer clients from doing negotiated bond underwriting for two years with those governments.
The board has repeatedly reminded dealers that G-37 also bars them from contributing "indirectly," like funneling a contribution to a particular candidate through certain PACs or parties.

NASD's report also reminds muni firms that broker-dealers must report the time-of-trade for interdealer transactions when they submit trade information, as required by MSRB, to the National Securities Clearing Corporation.

The report also reminds muni underwriters to send two copies of the final official statement and a completed form G-36 to MSRB within one business day after they get the final official statement from the issuer, and no later than 10 business days after a final purchase agreement.

The report also reminds bond dealers to use form G-37/38 when making their quarterly reports of contributions to MSRB. That expanded form covers a rule enacted by MSRB in March that requires dealers also to report their relationships with bond consultants.
